note: Cross-language conformance vectors. Encode a valid input with the given options (shuffle, set, dtype: 0 float32, 1 float16) and it must BYTE-MATCH the output; decode the output and the weights must be bit-exact float32 — for dtype 1, the half nearest each input float32 (ties to even), widened. Every invalid .namz must be rejected (empty/error, never crash). Decode each decodeOnly .namz and it must BYTE-MATCH its .nam. Encode each invalidNam .nam with its dtype and it must be refused.

invalid.name: bad-magic
invalid.why: magic corrupted

invalid.name: bad-version
invalid.why: formatVersion 9 (> 2) must be refused

invalid.name: bad-codec
invalid.why: codec 1 (deflate, reserved) must be refused

invalid.name: bad-dtype
invalid.why: dtype 1 (float16) on a float32 file: as halves its 12-byte payload is twice the 3 weights its lengths ask, so the length rule refuses it (dtype 2 and up are unknown: bad-dtype-2)

invalid.name: truncated
invalid.why: body truncated — exact-length check must reject

invalid.name: trailing-junk
invalid.why: extra bytes — exact-length check must reject

invalid.name: lying-metalen
invalid.why: metaLen far bigger than the buffer

invalid.name: empty
invalid.why: empty buffer

invalid.name: magic-only
invalid.why: header too short

invalid.name: version-zero
invalid.why: formatVersion 0 — only 1 and 2 are defined; the same bytes with 1 are decode-only/version-1

invalid.name: length-sum-wrap
invalid.why: lengths {2, 0xFFFFFFFF} over a one-float payload: the sum wraps to 1 in 32 bits, it is not 1

invalid.name: placeholder-past-segments
invalid.why: placeholder 1 with one segment: names no segment

invalid.name: placeholder-negative
invalid.why: placeholder -1: names no segment

invalid.name: placeholder-uint64
invalid.why: 9223372036854775808 fits an unsigned 64-bit integer, so it is a placeholder, and it names no segment

invalid.name: placeholder-duplicate-key
invalid.why: two "weights" keys in one object: the last one counts, and 5 names no segment

invalid.name: depth-129-scalar
invalid.why: 129 deep: an object around 128 arrays around a scalar (a scalar is 0)

invalid.name: depth-129-empty
invalid.why: 129 deep: an object around 127 arrays around an empty array (an empty one is 1)

invalid.name: depth-129-objects
invalid.why: 129 deep: an object around 127 objects around an empty object

invalid.name: depth-10000
invalid.why: 10,000 deep: refused without following it, and nothing may run out of stack on the way

invalid.name: depth-129-duplicate-key
invalid.why: 129 deep as written: depth counts the text, so a member a later duplicate key replaces still counts

invalid.name: skeleton-integer-overflow
invalid.why: an integer literal past every double: not a number the reference can hold

invalid.name: skeleton-utf16
invalid.why: a skeleton in UTF-16: JSON text in a .namz is UTF-8

invalid.name: skeleton-lone-surrogate
invalid.why: an escaped lone surrogate: no Unicode text, so not a JSON string the reference reads

invalid.name: payload-inf
invalid.why: a payload float that is +infinity: every payload float is a finite float32

invalid.name: payload-nan
invalid.why: a payload float that is NaN, in a segment no placeholder names: the rule is the payload's

invalid.name: bad-dtype-2
invalid.why: dtype 2: no such dtype — the payload would fit its lengths as halves, so only the dtype refuses it

invalid.name: f16-as-float32
invalid.why: a float16 file with dtype 0: as float32 its 16-byte payload holds 4 of the 8 weights its lengths ask

invalid.name: f16-truncated
invalid.why: a float16 payload one byte short: an odd length is no whole number of halves

invalid.name: f16-trailing-half
invalid.why: one half more than the lengths ask: a float16 payload is exactly sum(lengths) * 2 bytes

invalid.name: f16-short-lengths
invalid.why: lengths {1} over a payload of 3 halves: the lengths must sum to the payload

invalid.name: f16-payload-inf
invalid.why: a payload half that is -infinity: every half is finite

invalid.name: f16-payload-nan
invalid.why: a payload half that is NaN (0x7C01), in a segment no placeholder names: the rule is the payload's

decodeOnly.name: placeholder-minus-zero
decodeOnly.why: -0 is an integer literal, so it is a placeholder, and it names segment 0

decodeOnly.name: placeholder-fraction
decodeOnly.why: 1.0 has a fraction: a number, not a placeholder (segment 1 exists and stays unnamed)

decodeOnly.name: placeholder-exponent
decodeOnly.why: 0e0 has an exponent: a number, not a placeholder, printed as 0.0

decodeOnly.name: placeholder-past-uint64
decodeOnly.why: past every 64-bit integer: a double, not a placeholder

decodeOnly.name: placeholder-duplicate-key
decodeOnly.why: two "weights" keys in one object: the last one counts, and 0 names segment 0

decodeOnly.name: float-digits
decodeOnly.why: float32 payload values printed with the reference's own digits

decodeOnly.name: f16-widen
decodeOnly.why: float16 halves (2 byte planes) widen to the float32 of the same value, printed with the reference's digits: signed zeros, subnormals, the smallest normals, 65504; two segments, so the planes run across the whole payload

decodeOnly.name: f16-widen-noshuffle
decodeOnly.why: float16 halves (low byte first) widen to the float32 of the same value, printed with the reference's digits: signed zeros, subnormals, the smallest normals, 65504; two segments, so the planes run across the whole payload

decodeOnly.name: f16-version-1
decodeOnly.why: formatVersion 1 with dtype 1: no metadata length, float16 payload

invalidNam.name: weights-integer
invalidNam.why: an integer "weights" would be stored as a placeholder naming a segment that does not exist

invalidNam.name: weights-integer-nested
invalidNam.why: config.weights 0 would read back as the top-level weights array

invalidNam.name: weights-minus-zero
invalidNam.why: -0 is an integer literal, so it would be stored as a placeholder

invalidNam.name: depth-129
invalidNam.why: 129 deep: pack refuses what no reader would read back

invalidNam.name: depth-129-duplicate-key
invalidNam.why: 129 deep as written: depth counts the text, so a member a later duplicate key replaces still counts

invalidNam.name: utf16
invalidNam.why: a .nam in UTF-16: JSON text is UTF-8

invalidNam.name: lone-surrogate
invalidNam.why: an escaped lone surrogate: no Unicode text, so not a JSON string

invalidNam.name: weights-float32-overflow
invalidNam.why: 1e39 is a finite JSON number past the float32 range: the payload never stores an infinity

invalidNam.name: f16-overflow-tie
invalidNam.why: 65520 is the tie above the largest half 65504 and rounds to the even infinity: no half holds it

invalidNam.name: f16-overflow-flt-max
invalidNam.why: -FLT_MAX: a finite float32 past every half

invalidNam.name: f16-overflow-nested
invalidNam.why: one weight past half's range in a submodel: pack refuses the whole .nam
